# AiNexus AI Gateway

Enterprise-internal AI large model gateway: a pure HTTP transparent proxy (OpenAI compatible) that provides unified authentication, dynamic routing, and multi-channel disaster recovery, with an admin/internal user console; **no Token billing, no C-end user management**.

> Design taboos: do not introduce Spring AI / LangChain4j, and do not introduce WebFlux/Reactor. Only pass through HTTP messages and raw JSON/SSE streams.

---

## 1. Tech Stack

| Layer | Choice | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Language/runtime | JDK 21 (LTS) | Full virtual thread support |
| Web | Spring Boot 3.3.5 + Servlet(Tomcat) | `spring.threads.virtual.enabled=true`, request handling runs on virtual threads |
| Upstream forwarding | OkHttp3 4.12 | Dual-instance connection pool + streaming ResponseBody, see `OkHttpConfig` |
| Persistence | MySQL + MyBatis-Plus 3.5.7 | Channel main table `channel` + model binding table `channel_model` |
| Cache/concurrency | Redisson 3.34 | `RouteCacheService` versioned Token/route cache, channel round-robin RAtomicLong, channel concurrency RSemaphore |
| Auth | HandlerInterceptor | `Authorization: Bearer {Internal-Key}`, Mock whitelist + Redis set |

## 2. Architecture

```
Client (OpenAI SDK/curl)
   │  POST /v1/chat/completions   Authorization: Bearer {Internal-Key}
   ▼
InternalAuthInterceptor ── RouteCacheService looks up the Redis Token cache, returns 401 to block invalid Tokens
   ▼
ChatController ── parses only the two fields {model, stream}, request body kept as raw byte[]
   ▼
ChannelService ── RouteCacheService looks up Redis model → candidate channel cache
   │    Warmed up from MySQL channel + channel_model + gateway_token at startup and every 60 seconds; MySQL is not queried during requests
   │    When Redis is down, uses the local in-memory snapshot; one channel can bind multiple models; for the same model with multiple channels, allocation goes by priority first, then by weight
   │    Redis RAtomicLong…

A business and finance management system for IDC / cloud service providers. It covers the complete business loop of product management, order billing, automatic provisioning, invoicing, top-ups, distribution commissions, tickets, notifications, and more. It provides three front ends (an admin backend, a website portal, and a user console) and connects to upstream suppliers and third-party services through an extensible plugin mechanism.

| 🔔 Notifications | In-site messages, email, SMS (templates configurable) |
| ⚙️ Automation | Scheduled tasks, heartbeat monitoring, scheduled reconciliation, log archiving |

# DeepSeekBot

**Chinese** ｜ [English](https://github.com/BotHarness/DeepSeekBot/blob/HEAD/README.en.md)

**DeepSeekBot (DSB): an open-source alternative to GrokBot. A group of bots, each with its own identity, personality, and memory, working together.**

[Official site](https://deepseekbot.app) · [Promo video](#video) · [Install](#install) · [Features](#features) · [Release highlights](#releases) · [Differences from DS Bot](#deepseek-bot-projects) · [Community](#community) · [Docs](https://deepseekbot.app/docs/overview/)

A 3-minute look at DeepSeekBot: a group of bots with identities, personalities, and memories, getting things done together in a small town. Click the cover to play.

DeepSeekBot (DSB, short for DeepSeekBot, and not what it sounds like in Chinese, hmph) is an MIT-licensed open-source GrokBot alternative developed by BotHarness. It runs as a plugin inside [DeepSeek Harness (DSH)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness). You can create several bots, each responsible for research, writing, or coding, and chat with them privately, add them to groups, and assign them work just like coworkers. They remember you, work on schedules, and can reply to your messages under their own identities on Slack, Discord, Feishu / Lark, QQ, and WeChat.

Models use the providers and quotas you configure in DSH. When bots need to keep working in the background, the computer running DSH must stay online. It is a separate project from the similarly named DS Bot (npm `ds-bot`); see the differences [below](#deepseek-bot-projects).

## Install

In the DeepSeek Harness desktop app, go to Plugins → Add plugin, enter `deepseekbot@1.4.1`, then install and enable it. A “Bot mode” entry will appear in the sidebar. Haven't installed DSH yet? [Download the desktop app](https://www.deepseek.com/en/harness/) first.

DoYoungDo/clip.description: A small and beautiful tool for clipboard history
DoYoungDo/clip.body:
# Clip - Cross-platform Clipboard Manager

A system tray clipboard history manager that supports text and images, group management, translation, and LAN sharing.

## Features

- 📋 Automatically records clipboard history (text/images)
- 📁 Group management, saving different categories of content separately
- 🔍 Quick search of history records
- 🌈 Color format recognition and conversion (Hex ↔ RGB)
- 🌍 Integrates Baidu Translate / Youdao Translate
- 🔐 Translator keys are stored in the system credential store
- 🌐 Real-time clipboard sharing over LAN

## Build

```bash
# Quick build
./build.sh

# Specify platform
./script/build-mac-arm64.sh     # macOS Apple Silicon
./script/build-mac-amd64.sh     # macOS Intel
./script/build-linux-amd64.sh   # Linux
./script/build-win-amd64.sh     # Windows
```

> **Note**: Signing macOS apps requires purchasing a certificate. The author does not have one, so the packaged macOS apps are unsigned. To force-run them, see: [Common questions about installing unknown apps on mac](https://doyoungdo.github.io/essay/#/Other/mac_install_unknown_app)

## Usage

### Basic operations
- **Left click** - View history; click an entry to copy it
- **Right click** - Full menu and settings

### Group management
```
1. Copy the group name "Work Notes"
2. Right-click → ➕ Create group
3. Right-click the group → Activate
4. Clipboard content copied afterward is automatically saved to that group
```

### LAN sharing
**Scenario: Two computers share the clipboard with each other, and you can even "chat" by copying text through the menu**

**Computer A (server)**:
```
1. Right-click → Settings → LAN sharing → Enable
2. The address is automatically copied to the clipboard (e.g. 192.168.1.100:54321)
```

**Computer B (client)**:
```
1. Paste the address 192.168.1.100:54321
2. Right-click → Settings → LAN sharing → Connect to
3. Connected successfully!
```

**"Chat" example**:
```
Computer A: Copy "Dinner together tonight?"
Computer B: See the message marked [R] in the history
Computer B: Copy "Sure, what time?"
Computer A: See the reply [R] "Sure, what time?"
```

### Color conversion
```
1. Right-click → Settings → Auto-detect colors ✓
2. Copy #FF5733
3. Right-click that entry → the "Copy Hex / Copy RGB" options appear
4. After clicking, you get 255,87,51
```

### Translation
```
1. Copy the translator key to the clipboard
   - Baidu Translate:…
```

MAD-Producer/Kilonova.body:
# Motion Studio

Motion Studio is an open-source motion graphics editor for desktop. It organizes the creative workflow with layers, keyframes, curves, nodes, and GPU compositing, aiming to let motion design, compositing effects, and real-time preview work together in the same project.

The project is in ongoing development. Current development and automated verification focus on Windows, Linux, and macOS desktop. The desktop version already provides usable layer editing, timeline, curve, and node effect workflows. The Android version is no longer maintained. Its historical source code and manual build tools are retained, but automatic builds, device testing, and APK releases have been disabled.

## Current Capabilities

| Area | Provided | Still being improved |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Layers & timeline | Layer hierarchy, clip moving, trimming, splitting, parent-child relationships, blend modes, track masks | More complete media management and advanced timeline workflows |
| Animation & curves | Keyframes for position, anchor, scale, rotation, opacity, and effect parameters; value curves and speed curves | More curve editing handles, expression references, and complex easing |
| Node effects | Desktop node canvas, type checking, connections, grouping, compiling, real-time preview, bound layer effects | Multi-pass node graphs, custom WGSL workflows, and mobile node graph editing |
| Effect library | Built-in effect packs, category search, parameter animation, `.msfx` import/export | More complete effect categories, previews, and third-party pack management |
| Camera & 3D | 2D/3D layers, cameras, parent-child relationships, top and side views | More complete spatial controller and camera tools |
| Media | Image, video, and audio import; synchronized audio playback on desktop; desktop packages with FFmpeg support MP4 encoding | Audio-only preview and audible scrubbing |
| Automation | Desktop MCP, command batches, revision checks, undo, and read-only sessions | Model provider and chat panel integration |

Effect and node implementations are Motion Studio's own code. Some parameters and visual behaviors are still approximate implementations. For specific boundaries, see [Built-in Effects and Font API](https://github.com/MAD-Producer/Kilonova/blob/HEAD/engineering/host-api/official-motion-effects.md) and [Node Authoring Plan](https://github.com/MAD-Producer/Kilonova/blob/HEAD/desktop/NODE-AUTHORING.md).

deshark42/agent-notes.body:
# Agent Notes

An Agent Note is an RFC-style document written by an agent that records the reasoning behind a long-term decision and the alternatives that were rejected.

This repository organizes the Agent Notes system from [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH) into a template that other code projects can adopt. The contract is at [`.agents/notes/README.md`](https://github.com/deshark42/agent-notes/blob/HEAD/.agents/notes/README.md).

Compared with the original DSH, this template removes DSH-specific content (package paths, pnpm/run-gates, GH stack; skills drop the `dsh-` prefix), uses the `npm run verify` aggregate gate instead, keeps only the Chinese contract, and rewrites the root `AGENTS.md` as a neutral version.

## Template contents

```text
AGENTS.md       agent instructions: contract pointer, commands, check selection
.agents/notes/  note tree, contract, and lifecycle/class descriptions
.agents/skills/ archive workflow, pre-push check selection strategy
scripts/        gates: note path/class, header/sections, sealed archive
package.json    npm run verify aggregate script, one script per gate
```

Note paths follow `{lifecycle}/{class}/yyyy-mm-dd-topic-title.md`:

- `proposed/` — proposals under review before implementation.
- `implemented/` — delivered decisions, kept in sync with the code's facts.
- `rejected/` — rejected proposals; kept only while their reasoning still prevents a tempting mistake.
- `archived/{class}/` — sealed implemented notes; permanently frozen and recorded in `manifest.json`.

## Usage

There are two ways to use it:

1. **Create a new repository from the template**: click **Use this template** → **Create a new repository**, or go directly to [github.com/deshark42/agent-notes/generate](https://github.com/deshark42/agent-notes/generate), to get a new repository containing the complete Agent Notes system.
2. **Copy into an existing repository**: copy all files from this repository into the target repository. If the target already has a `README.md` or `AGENTS.md`, merge the content instead of overwriting it.

After that:

1. Rewrite the opening paragraph of `AGENTS.md` to describe the target project; Take this…

helsome/folio.body:
# Folio

  Research markets, understand your exposure, and maintain evidence-based judgments over time, with a clear view of what has changed.

> In one sentence: a market terminal tells you **What happened**; Folio's Agent helps you answer **Why does this matter to you**, records **What did you believe before**, and keeps tracking **What changed**.

## Our Product

Folio is a desktop research environment built for public market investors. It combines a calm, tidy financial workspace with an Agent copilot. The Agent can retrieve structured market data, explain evidence, and carry research forward into investment theses, alerts, and portfolio decisions.

Folio is local-first: sessions, credentials, and research state are stored on your device by default. Market data and model providers are explicit integrations, not hidden dependencies.

> Folio is a research and decision-support tool. By design it is read-only and provides no order placement or trading capability.

## Screenshots

## Core Features

### Research Workspace

- Watchlists, quotes, candlestick charts, financial statements, news, and security overviews.
- Three-column desktop layout: navigation, market workspace, and Agent copilot. A persistent asset tab bar at the top (Candles / Statements / News / Reports) lets you switch perspective in one click from any page.
- Compare 2–4 securities across valuation, growth, profit margins, ROE, dividends, returns, ratings, and momentum.
- Data freshness is visible. Missing values are shown as `—` and are never guessed.

### Out-of-the-Box Sample Data (Offline Fallback)

- When no market data provider or LLM is connected, Today, the portfolio overview, market pulse, events, and the daily brief automatically show built-in sample data, so the app is complete from the first launch.
- All sample content carries a prominent "Sample Data" badge (with a setup-guidance tooltip). Error messages are kept in the underlying state, and real data overrides the samples as soon as it is available.
- Codes outside the sample set (such as `0700.HK`) keep honest empty or error states and never fabricate data.

### Deep Research

- Start research on a focused security with one click.
- Parallel capability calls with bounded concurrency, timeouts, cancellation, and honest partial-failure states.
- Structured data package → Agent synthesis → evidence-based `ResearchReport`.
- Reports include a stance, confidence level, sections, bull case, bear case, catalysts, and risks, plus links from each claim to the capability execution records behind it.

### Agent Copilot

- Persistent sessions and streaming answers powered by the Pi Agent runtime.
- Model and thinking-level controls, stop/cancel, workspace context, and structured market and portfolio cards.
- Markdown answers support headings, lists, tables, links, and code blocks.
- Internal synthesis sessions do not appear in the visible conversation history.

### Agent Evaluation and Observability

- Built-in Evaluation Center: view experiments, baselines, model comparisons, failure modes, case details, and human feedback.

# Learn Ukrainian

**Мова -- душа народу** | Language is the soul of a nation

A free, open-source Ukrainian language course from A1 to C2, based on the **Ukrainian State Standard 2024** and aligned with **CEFR**.

**[Start Learning](https://learn-ukrainian.github.io)**

---

## What is this?

A comprehensive Ukrainian language curriculum with 1,778 modules across 22 tracks:

- **6 core CEFR levels** (A1 -- C2) covering grammar, vocabulary, and communication
- **16 specialization tracks** -- history, biographies, literature, professional Ukrainian, folk culture, Old East Slavic, and Ruthenian
- **Theory-first approach** -- understand grammar deeply, not just memorize phrases
- **Interactive exercises** -- quizzes, matching, fill-in-the-blank, error correction
- **Cultural context** -- decolonization perspective, authentic Ukrainian sources
- **100% free** -- no ads, no subscriptions, no paywalls

## Tracks

### Core Levels

proteus-vue/proteus.description: Proteus: Vue cross-platform compilation framework (WeChat Mini Program Skyline + Web). One set of Vue source code, compiled into forms for a thousand platforms.
proteus-vue/proteus.body:
# Proteus: a semantically converged cross-platform application framework

> **One semantic model. Any render engine. Zero native glue.**
> One semantic kernel, any render engine, any native capability. Business code talks only to the semantic layer. The rendering substrate, compiler, host container, and execution carrier are all pluggable.
>
> **Not cross-platform translation, but a cross-platform operating system: semantics are the kernel, backends are drivers.**

[Methodology philosophy](#方法论哲学统一语义收敛) · [Killer features](#杀手特性) · [Quick start](https://github.com/proteus-vue/proteus/blob/HEAD/docs/getting-started.md) · [Architecture overview](https://github.com/proteus-vue/proteus/blob/HEAD/docs/board-inventory.md) · [External positioning](https://github.com/proteus-vue/proteus/blob/HEAD/docs/proteus-positioning-v3.md)

---

## Why the name Proteus (origin of the name)

**Proteus** is a sea god in ancient Greek mythology, a herdsman of Poseidon, known as the “Old Man of the Sea.” In the *Odyssey*, when he is captured on the island of Pharos, he transforms into a lion, a serpent, a wild boar, flowing water, and a tree. The English word **protean (ever-changing)** comes from his name. He also knows the past, present, and future.

| Proteus's divine attributes | The framework's differentiating advantages |
|---|---|
| **Shapeshifting**: one being takes on many forms | **One semantics, many platform forms**: the same business semantics become Vue DOM / native / Flutter / Skia / Mini Programs. The form changes, the essence stays the same |
| **Prophecy**: foreseeing the future | **Compile-time first**: the semantic IR is validated and converged at build time. Anything detectable at compile time is never left until runtime |
| **Constant essence**: after transformation, still Proteus | **Constant semantics**: business code depends only on the semantic kernel. All platform differences are pushed down into backend implementation details |
| **Omniscience**: knows past, present, and future | **Verifiable**: every SPI layer has conformance gates. Whether a backend implementation complies can be checked mechanically and enforced by CI |
| **Manifest as light**: transformation is revelation, nothing can hide | **Transparent compilation**: conversion rules are self-describing (an AI manual), and decision traces can be enumerated and traced back. No black boxes |

## Methodology philosophy: Unified Semantic Convergence

> **Proteus does not do cross-platform translation. Instead, it defines a platform-independent semantic kernel, and all platform differences are pushed down into “backend implementation details.”**

Core formula:

```
Any cross-platform problem = semantic definition (done by the framework) + backend implementation (done by the platform)
```…

An AI Agent translates PO files and creates diffs, and a human reviews them as Markdown.
When repeated revisions finalize the translations, they are submitted to Transifex.
For example, start the work by asking like this:

> Pick one file from tutorial, improve the existing translations, and translate the untranslated parts.

   The glossary uses `translation_ja` as the standard, and checks `pos` and `notes` to confirm the context in which each term applies.
   Also read related tutorial and library descriptions to choose style and terminology.
   Find translation examples in the current POs registered in `.tx/config`, and do not adopt untranslated, fuzzy, or obsolete entries.

2. **Improve existing translations and translate untranslated parts.**
   Review mistranslations, omissions, unnatural word order, and punctuation.
   Preserve the original text, references, formulas, and the calculation formulas or output in code examples; translate comments in code examples as needed.

shuishuipingan/qoder2api-hub.body:

## Features

- **Three protocols**: OpenAI Chat Completions, Responses API (Codex), Anthropic Messages (Claude Code)
- **Dual-region multi-account**: the domestic and international editions have separate account pools and egress, with automatic region selection based on the model; account round-robin, session affinity, and failure cooldown with account switching
- **Client-free login**: OAuth device authorization, PAT import, or direct import of credentials already logged in via the local official client

git clone https://github.com/shuishuipingan/qoder2api-hub.git

skyle1995/NetworkAuth.description: A network authentication system developed in Golang
skyle1995/NetworkAuth.body:
# NetworkAuth (Network Authorization Service)

NetworkAuth (网络授权服务) is a backend system focused on application authentication, API interface management, and dynamic logic distribution. Developed in Go, it provides core services such as application management, API interface management, variable management, and user authentication.

## Features

### 🚀 Core Features
- **Application management**: Supports create, read, update, and delete operations for applications, plus version management, status control, and key management
- **API interface management**: Supports API interface configuration with multiple encryption algorithms (RC4, RSA, 易加密, etc.)
- **Variable management**: A standalone variable system that supports create, read, update, and delete operations, as well as alias management
- **Function management**: Supports custom function code management, which can be bound to specific applications or used globally
- **User management**: A complete user authentication and permission management system
- **System settings**: Flexible system configuration and parameter management
- **System initialization**: Provides guided data table initialization and default settings injection
- **Log auditing**: Detailed login logs and operation logs to help keep the system secure

### 🔧 Technical Features
- **RESTful API**: Standard REST API interface design
- **JWT authentication**: A security authentication mechanism based on JWT
- **Multiple encryption algorithms**: Supports RC4, RSA, RSA dynamic, 易加密, and other encryption methods
- **Database support**: Compatible with MySQL and SQLite (via GORM)
- **Redis cache**: Integrates Redis cache to improve performance (optional)
- **Logging system**: Complete log recording and management with log rotation (Logrus + Lumberjack)
- **Configuration management**: A flexible configuration system based on Viper
- **Command-line tool**: A powerful CLI management tool based on Cobra

## Tech Stack

- **Language**: Go 1.25.0
- **Web framework**: Gin
- **Database ORM**: GORM
- **Cache**: Redis (optional)
- **Authentication**: JWT + captcha
- **Logging**: Logrus + Lumberjack
- **Configuration management**: Viper
- **Command line**: Cobra
- **Encryption**: Custom encryption toolkit

## Project Structure

```
NetworkAuth/
├── cmd/                    # Cobra command-line tool definitions
├── config/                 # Configuration file models and validation logic
├── constants/              # Global constant definitions (version numbers, status codes, etc.)
├── controllers/            # Controller layer (handles HTTP requests)
├── database/               # Database connection, migration, and default data population
├── middleware/…
```

yushui2022/easy-coding-agents.body:
**ECA Desktop 0.34.1 Windows Preview**: The desktop project is located in `desktop/` and supports multiple projects and concurrent sessions, a main conversation with side-chat attachments, web preview, an interactive PowerShell terminal, and on-demand modification review. It shares the Python core and project data with the CLI. [Installation, development, and acceptance notes](https://github.com/yushui2022/easy-coding-agents/blob/HEAD/docs/desktop/README.md). The npm launcher provides both `eca` and the compatible command `ecs`.

A new agent taking over should first read the [complete handoff document](https://github.com/yushui2022/easy-coding-agents/blob/HEAD/HANDOFF.md). It covers local machine paths, the status of uncommitted code, dependencies, the G-drive cache, packaging and updates, testing, and the terracotta UI conventions.

The main agent has no default limit on response turns or on output-truncation recovery attempts; you can interrupt it with Ctrl+C. Explicit limits in older configurations remain in effect. To remove both limits, run `ecs --max-turns 0 --output-recovery-limit 0`. For the difference between the per-response model output limit, sub-agent limits, and shared budgets, see [output and continuous execution configuration](https://github.com/yushui2022/easy-coding-agents/blob/HEAD/docs/OUTPUT_LIMITS.md).

---

ECA (Easy Coding Agent) is a programming assistant where you configure the model yourself. It offers a CLI and a Windows desktop entry point, both sharing the Python core. It can read and search projects, edit files, and run commands, and it saves full sessions and file-modification records locally within the project. The desktop installer bundles its own runtime; running the CLI requires Python 3.11+.

It focuses on three things: **changes can be inspected, work can be resumed, and memory has sources.** You can review diffs before allowing writes, resume sessions after an interruption, and inspect or revert changes produced by file tools.

> It is currently suitable for personal trials, development, and research. The core mechanisms have automated tests, but stability on real complex tasks is still being verified, and it does not yet match the feature coverage and reliability of mature coding CLIs.

Large-repository navigation: `/related SYMBOL` shows the definition and Python call/import candidates. The model's `code_search`, `repo_map`, and `code_relations` support directory filtering and incremental read statistics. [Usage and validation boundaries](https://github.com/yushui2022/easy-coding-agents/blob/HEAD/docs/REPOSITORY_NAVIGATION.md).

z7ping/agent-lens.description: See every observable action of your AI coding agents. · Trace your agents, down to every tool and MCP.
z7ping/agent-lens.body:
> [!IMPORTANT]
> AgentLens 1.0 is currently in Alpha. 1.0 is a Clean Rebuild centered on Canonical Observation + Evidence; 0.x serves only as a verified reference for behavior and design and is not part of the 1.0 runtime.

## Why AgentLens

Codex, Claude Code, Pi, Hermes, OpenCode and other tools scatter sessions, tool calls, and capability configuration across JSONL, SQLite, Hooks, and config directories. AgentLens organizes these **observable facts** into a unified, traceable view to help you answer:

- What did the agent just do, and at which step did it fail?
- What turns, tool calls, and lifecycle events did a long task go through?
- Does a given conclusion come from historical records, native tail-reading, or a Runtime Hook?
- Which Skills, MCPs, and Plugins are installed on this machine, and which have actually been invoked?
- Which data is complete, which has only partial coverage, and which sources are currently unavailable?

AgentLens shows behavior that the sources can prove. It does not claim to read hidden reasoning, and it does not dress up speculation as fact.

## Get started in 30 seconds

### Desktop app

Go to [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/z7ping/agent-lens/releases) and download the installer that matches your platform and architecture. **A source development build is not the same as a released version; rely on the files the corresponding Release actually provides.**

- Windows x64: `AgentLens-<version>-Setup-x64.exe`
- macOS: choose the DMG the Release actually provides for Apple Silicon (arm64) / Intel (x64)
- Linux x64: AppImage or DEB; the current build does not provide a Linux arm64 installer

The desktop app and the npm version share the same Runtime, default data directory, and data model; installing both will not create a second database.

### npm / CLI

Requires Node.js 22.23.0 or later:

```bash
npm install -g @z7ping/agent-lens
agent-lens setup
agent-lens service start
```

Then open <http://127.0.0.1:56789>.

`setup` performs one-time initialization only; it does not automatically start the long-running Daemon, nor does it enable login auto-start by default. Use `agent-lens start` when you need foreground debugging.

Check runtime status:

```bash
agent-lens status
agent-lens doctor
```
